title: SSE heartbeat jitter & trace-boundary alignment for function-callable streaming
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Problem: Clients using our SSE streaming endpoint see correlated reconnect storms during transient infra events (e.g., load balancer reconnections). Reconnect storms cause duplicate partial function-call frames and make it hard to deterministically reassemble structured JSON outputs and tool/function-call boundaries. Goal: implement a combined server and client-side approach to reduce thundering reconnects, provide robust chunk attribution (trace IDs + sequence offsets), and improve function-call/structured-output resumption semantics for polyfilled environments (EventSource shims, ReadableStream adaptations).
design_notes: Introduce optional heartbeat event (event: heartbeat) emitted every server_heartbeat_ms but with server-side jitter of +/- 30% to avoid synchronized reconnections.

Attach a per-session trace_id and per-chunk attribution metadata header (X-Chunk-Trace / chunk_seq) emitted as SSE comment lines (e.g., :trace=<id>, :seq=42) to ensure polyfills can access provenance without requiring non-standard headers.

On reconnect, client provides last-acknowledged chunk_seq and trace_id as query parameters (resume_trace, resume_seq). Server validates trace_id and returns delta from that sequence if available; if trace mismatch, server returns a small sanity snapshot event (event: snapshot) with a compact reassembly token to enable client-state reconciliation.

Merge function-call boundaries: function-call frames are assigned boundary markers with boundary_id and a finality flag. If a reconnect occurs mid-boundary, resume semantics must prefer server-side dedup + continuation rather than naive re-emission to avoid duplicate tool calls.

Compatibility: For EventSource polyfills that strip comment lines, also emit a short JSON envelope as a `meta` event containing the same trace/seq metadata so both native and shimmed clients can recover.
Observability: emit metrics for reconnect_rate, duplicates_detected, resume_failures, and average_resume_latency. Add logging hooks that include trace_id and chunk_seq for postmortem correlation.

Backoff negotiation: server should accept a client-specified connector hint (resume_backoff_hint) to allow clients to apply jittered exponential backoff; server will use this for admission when under load.
Security: ensure X-Chunk-Trace is ephemeral and rotates per-session to avoid long-lived identifiers. Do not emit PII in snapshot events.
acceptance_criteria: SSE endpoint emits heartbeat events with randomized jitter; synthetic client test shows reduced reconnect alignment under flood test (target: 5x reduction in synchronized reconnects).
Chunk provenance metadata (trace_id, chunk_seq) is present and accessible to native EventSource and two common polyfills (Mozilla polyfill and Node eventsource).

Clients can resume mid-stream by providing resume_trace and resume_seq; server returns consistent continuation or snapshot token. Resume failure rate < 0.5% on benchmarked runs with transient 1s disconnects.
Function-call boundaries are never duplicated after a successful resume (benchmarks with fcall-heavy prompts show zero duplicate tool invocations post-resume in 1000 trials).
Metrics emitted to the console and internal telemetry with tags: trace_id, region, model_slug, and reconnect_type. Dashboards updated to show reconnect hotspots and resume success rate.
Design doc and API compatibility notes published to Confluence; README updated for SDKs with recommended resume handling and example polyfill code snippets.
tasks: Spec API additions: query params (resume_trace, resume_seq, resume_backoff_hint) and SSE meta event format (OWNER: Liam Hart).
Server runtime: heartbeat generator with jitter + chunk metadata emitter (OWNER: Priya Menon).
Resume reassembly: server-side delta store and snapshot generator for short-lived resumes (OWNER: Diego Ramos).
Client SDK: Node and browser examples for resume handshake + polyfill compatibility (OWNER: Mei Chen).
Integration tests: chaos tests to simulate load balancer flaps and assert resume behavior (OWNER: QA Team).
Dashboard: new telemetry panels and alerts for reconnect_rate and resume_failures (OWNER: observability team).
Security review & perf review ahead of runtime-1.20 cut (OWNER: Security: Jordan Blake; Perf: Arjun Singh).
decisions: Use SSE comment lines for lightweight provenance to minimize changes to existing clients while also emitting an explicit `meta` event for polyfills that strip comments.
Per-session trace_id will be base62-encoded 12-char token rotated on session restart; not persisted beyond 24 hours.
Server will prefer sending delta continuation when resume_trace matches and sequence gap <= 500 chunks; otherwise server issues snapshot event and a short reassembly token.
Do not change existing HTTP API surface; resume params are optional and backward-compatible.
Opted for server-side admission control rather than forcing client backoff to preserve low-latency for premium tiers.
